Antonio Linares@alc2022

$HIMS is down 80% from the ATHs.

But peptides are moving towards approval. I believe this is the first domino in a profoundly consequential chain of events that could make $HIMS worth $2,000 per share intrinsically by 2030.

1/ BPC-157 and other generic peptides get approved.

Millions of people start taking them. They see results. And then they ask the obvious question:

What else can I take?

2/ They ask that question on the platform that already owns the relationship with them.

$HIMS is one of the largest D2C healthcare platforms on Earth, with a vertically integrated supply chain.

Vertical integration wins on cost.

Cost wins the customer.

The customer reinforces the economies of scale.

3/ Every customer becomes a source of biomarker data.

Over time, that dataset compounds across multiple dimensions:

More patients. More biomarkers. More longitudinal measurements. More intervention-outcome pairs.

Every new customer makes the machine smarter.

Every improvement in the machine makes the platform more valuable to the next customer.

The intelligence compounds as a function of scale.

4/ Eventually, the dataset could reach a level of granularity that enables $HIMS to leverage AI to design personalised peptide interventions at scale.

The objective function is remarkably simple:

Maximise patient outcomes while driving the marginal cost of healthcare down.

Instead of spending billions designing one molecule for millions of people, we begin designing the optimal combination of molecules for each individual.

The pharmaceutical business model gets inverted.

5/ This is the scenario in which I believe $HIMS becomes worth $2,000 per share intrinsically by 2030.

The market begins to recognise the company as the infrastructure behind an entirely new AI scaling law:

Life extension per token.

As the intelligence becomes increasingly predictive, the centre of gravity of the pharmaceutical industry shifts.

Value migrates away from the molecules themselves and towards the intelligence capable of designing them, trained on the deepest longitudinal biomarker dataset on Earth.

The molecule is the output.

The intelligence is the asset.

6/ This sets off a global race to either own or access that intelligence.

If you're a pharmaceutical company operating outside this intelligence layer, your competitors could design better interventions at a fraction of your cost.

If you're a consumer operating outside it, those with access to the intelligence could experience better health outcomes and potentially live longer than you.

In both cases, the cost of not participating compounds.

7/ This is how $HIMS could eventually become the most valuable subscription service on Earth.

Much like operating without $PLTR could eventually become analogous to operating without electricity, living outside the $HIMS OS could become an increasingly consequential disadvantage.

The more predictive the intelligence becomes, the higher the opportunity cost of not subscribing.

Except this time, what the machine produces isn't economic efficiency.

It isn't productivity.

It's time.

The most valuable and finite resource in human existence.

Could the markets have bottomed yet? Potentially yes.

But is it confirmed? No.

The markets are SLOWLY showing signs of an early bottom, but not yet.

We have the first flush down to oversold territories. Now we look for divergences to form to confirm a bottom. We do NOT have divergences yet formed, so markets can STILL go down if the algo's are not ready yet.

So what should you do?

1. Still take it slow, buy the red days no matter what - rain or shine, on schedule, with your paychecks every few weeks

2. I would also buy the dip on defensive stocks as well - this will help keep you balanced in case markets extend into bear season. Look for our main hedges like oil, consumer staples, and other fundamentally strong stocks

3. Do not rush - keep it steady. Zoom out and plan on what you will do if the markets come down another - 5% - 15%.

All in all, remember. Do not worry about red days. These are the opportunities you are looking for to become rich in the future.

Antonio Linares@alc2022
05:03 SGT quoteInvesting
All value accrues to the data layer
@ · 24 Nov 2026, 02:01 SGT
Most people still treat AI, biotech, and clinical longevity medicine as separate markets.

In isolation, each one hits a hard ceiling:

1) AI models run out of scraped text and cannot validate biological predictions without real human outcomes.

2) Biotech keeps inventing targeted molecules while relying on blunt, population-average medicine to deploy them.

3) Personalized medicine works in high-touch longevity clinics, yet cannot scale synthesis across hundreds of biomarkers and therapies by hand.

Connect all three into a single loop and each layer clears the others' bottleneck.

Biotech supplies the interventions, clinical care personalizes delivery and tracks real-world outcomes, and AI compounds every patient's response into sharper decisions.

Because very few people speak all three languages fluently, this intersection holds some of the biggest opportunities of the next decade.

I'm spending a lot of time personally going deep on this space and sharing what I find here. Follow along if you want to learn too.

The bears are having their moment.

After predicting a top in the AI trade every month for the last 4 years, the bears finally got their moment last week.

However, in 3 to 6 months, we are going to look back at this correction and realize it was just that: a correction.

There is a widespread narrative right now that Nvidia, $NVDA, is quite literally going to collapse. This is a stock that was trading at a record high on October 6th, worth nearly $6 trillion, and the inventor of the most advanced chips in the world (it's not even close).

That's how deeply pessimistic sentiment has become over the last seven weeks.

Even if Nvidia produced half as much revenue as they are guiding for their next fiscal year, this company would still produce close to $400 billion in annual revenue.

Meanwhile, the S&P 500 has posted three consecutive quarters with earnings growth above 25% and eight straight quarters of double-digit growth.

And, sentiment flipped so quickly that the S&P 500 closed the week 4.1 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average on Friday. Not even 2020 and 2008 saw such an occurrence.

The reality is that AI truly is the "next big thing" and the AI buildout is only accelerating.

Bears will sound smart, bulls will make money.

TRUMP: I PREDICTED THE STOCK MARKET WOULD CRASH IF THE DEMOCRATS WON THE MIDTERMS, LOOK WHAT HAPPENED

Trump doesn’t like that the markets are down this dramatically given he is the President, but it also seems pretty clear that if he can blame the Democrats, it’s a way for him to show voters that going against him during the midterms was a horrible idea.

Usually whenever markets would fall 0.4% this year, much less the 4% drop on Friday, Trump would post something bullish to flip the narrative.

On Friday, he did a 2 hour press conference and basically said nothing about the markets, almost as if he didn’t even care, likely to send a message about the Democrats winning.

The US equity market experienced just one of its sharpest sell-offs on record:

The S&P 500 fell -11.6% from its October 6th peak in just 33 trading days, placing the decline among the 15 fastest corrections since 1928.

By comparison, at the start of the 2022 bear market, it took 34 sessions for the index to fall at least -10%.

During the 2020 pandemic selloff, the same decline took just 6 trading days, while in March 2025 it took 17 sessions.

Overall, 4 of the 15 fastest corrections since 1928 have occurred over the last 6 years.

Meanwhile, 94% of S&P 500 stocks were down last week, with 111 declining by at least -10%.

At the same time, 11 stocks in the index were down by at least -20%.

Market sentiment has become extremely pessimistic.

00:44 SGTInvesting
One market rule that has saved me from major losses and helped me capture some of my biggest winners:

Avoid buying stocks below their 200-day moving average.

The 200-day moving average represents roughly 10 months of trading history and helps identify the long-term trend. Once a major uptrend or downtrend is established, it often takes time to reverse.

You might miss the initial 15-20% move, sometimes even more. But that's the premium I'm willing to pay to reduce downside risk and avoid wasting time in prolonged downtrends.

The goal isn't to catch the exact bottom. It's to identify quality market leaders and participate in the next major uptrend, which can sometimes deliver 80-100% returns or more.

Take $GOOGL as an example. Notice how price behaves around the 200-day SMA during major trend changes.

Reclaiming the 9/21-day EMAs and 50-day SMA can be early signs of improving price action. Eventually, reclaiming the 200-day SMA, supported by improving relative strength and volume, provides stronger evidence that a new uptrend may be developing.

An Amazon memo details strategy for agentic AI shopping, per Reuters.

It currently blocks AI agents from platform. Plans to build a “World Product Graph”, basically a search engine for every product on Earth (even ones Amazon doesn't sell).

The memo writes that “whoever owns the product data owns the agent."

Currently, 57% of shoppers starting product research begin on Google (vs. 16%). However, if shoppers know exactly what they want, then 41% start on Amazon (vs. 23% on Google).

A “World Product Graph” also meant to address shortcomings of Amazon’s Rufus chatbot:

▫️”Many Rufus answers are factually wrong or incomplete, but customers lack expertise to detect these errors.”
▫️Rufus did about 83M searches a week, and the memo calls running them “expensive”.

One made-up customer quote explains problem trying to be solved: “I used to spend an hour on Reddit figuring this stuff out.”
